grand_strategy.reading:
Armenia is a state that lost its war in 2020, its enclave in 2023 and its
patron's guarantee in between, and is now trying to buy a settlement and a new
set of protectors with the only coin it has left: the use of its territory. The
strategy is unusually coherent for a small state - peace with Azerbaijan first,
then a transport role (TRIPP, the Turkish rail link, Iran), then the EU and the US
as insurance, with Russia kept in the tent by gas, the base and the EAEU until the
other pieces hold. That is Luttwak's logic of the weaker party, which survives by
making itself useful to several stronger ones at once.

The paradoxes all sit at the joints. The treaty needs a constitution the June 2026
majority could not deliver; the corridor that ends the blockade is an American-run
concession through its own south; the pivot from Russia is financed by trade with
Russia; the EU law raises the cost of the gas that keeps the lights on. The
domestic fight with the Church and Karapetyan is not a side show: it is the same
contest, because the people who would vote 'no' to the preamble are also the ones
Moscow courts. Pashinyan's election win shows the public chose the pivot over the
nostalgia, but not with the margin the strategy needs, which is why the next real
test is not Moscow or Baku but a referendum with no date.

stances.note: Until 2023 the pair was the ontology's reference case of 'adversary'. Since the loss of Nagorno-Karabakh (offensive of 19-20 Sep 2023, more than 100,000 people fled in ten days) Yerevan has accepted Baku's terms: treaty text agreed 13 Mar 2025, initialled in Washington on 8 Aug 2025, Minsk Group dissolved on 1 Sep 2025, transit ban lifted 21 Oct 2025, Pashinyan saying in October 2026 that 'peace is established'. Not 'partner' because the treaty is unsigned and conditional on a constitutional referendum, 19 Armenians are in Baku's prisons (Vardanyan, 20 years, Feb 2026), the Shaki shooting of Oct 2026 is open, and the Armenian opposition calls the preamble demand imposed by Baku. Not 'adversary' because Armenia seeks recognition of borders, not Azerbaijan's defeat. Asymmetry risk: Baku is likely to grade Armenia lower than 'rival' warming; its card is not yet written. Serbia's card grades Azerbaijan 'partner' (strategic partners, defence contract, gas); it holds nothing on Armenia, so there was nothing to mirror for this pair.

stances.note: Russia is still Armenia's treaty ally on paper (CSTO membership, which the dataset turns into an 'ally' floor; the 1997 friendship treaty; the 102nd base in Gyumri, lease to 2044) and its largest trading partner (35.5% of foreign trade), gas monopolist and remittance source. In structure it is no longer an alliance: the CSTO has been frozen since February 2024, Pashinyan says Armenia will not return in the next five years and that he would be 'very pleased' to be expelled, Russian border guards left Zvartnots on 31 Jul 2024, Russia's share of arms procurement fell from over 96% to about 10%, Pashinyan says 'we are not Russia's allies on Ukraine' and that the Gyumri base 'adds nothing', and Moscow answers with import bans (spring 2026), a notified threat to denounce the gas agreement (27 May 2026) and Medvedev's 'second Ukraine' (Oct 2026). Carnegie reports Putin now deals with Pashinyan 'as a partner, albeit a problematic one, not as an ally'. Hence 'partner' (transactional, unaligned) rather than 'reluctant_ally' or 'rival'. Bond - grievance: the lasting wound is Russia's non-intervention in 2021-23 and the Karabakh loss, laid on top of deep economic and human ties (a large diaspora and workers in Russia). Armenia is not Russia's mortal enemy and Russia is not Armenia's.

stances_toward.note: Mirror of Armenia's reading. The only open friendly border: gas-for-electricity swap to 2030, the Meghri-Nordooz bridge and Kajaran-Agarak road of the North-South corridor, and Mirzoyan's visit to Tehran on 5-6 Oct 2026. Iran's exposure to US pressure limits what Yerevan can build on it, and Tehran is uneasy about an American-run route (TRIPP) on its border. Partner, not ally. The build's 'partner of an adversary's ally' warning (Armenia has a US strategic partnership and TRIPP) is answered by geography: Yerevan is Iran's only open friendly border and Tehran tolerates the US-run route rather than lose it. Bond - none (the old support for Armenia against Baku is policy, not kinship).

stances_toward.note: Carnegie's reading is Moscow's: Putin now deals with Pashinyan 'as a partner, albeit a problematic one, not as an ally'. The paper alliance survives (CSTO membership frozen by Yerevan since Feb 2024, the Gyumri base to 2044, the 1997 treaty) but Moscow's own conduct is transactional and punitive - import bans before the June 2026 election, a notified threat to denounce the gas agreement if Armenia joins the EU (27 May 2026), Medvedev's 'second Ukraine' (5 Oct 2026), Putin's offer to leave Gyumri 'even tomorrow'. Cooling. Bond - affinity: Orthodox Christian, Soviet and diaspora ties that Moscow still counts on, while Yerevan's own bond is grievance.
